title: Orchid MedTech — on‑prem integration scratchpad
call_summary: 30-min intro with Orchid MedTech infra lead (Raj), clinical product lead (Tara), and their IT security. High-level ask: deploy Redwood Private within their hospital network to power a triage assistant. They want air-gapped option, HSM-based key management, and evidence of FIPS-140 compliance. Concern: no outbound internet from enclave.
notes:
Context: Orchid is an early adopter in medtech devices (point-of-care triage tablets). Sensitive PHI flows; legal requires data never leave hospital VPC. They prefer a customer-managed control plane (or at minimum private control plane). Key phrases from call: 'zero exfil', 'FIPS', 'device-level inference for 10k daily sessions', 'predictable latency under 250ms for single-turn queries'.

Technical sketch: target hardware = 2x A100 80GB per rack for PoC (they have HPE servers), possibility to evaluate 1x H100 later. OS images will be tightly locked down; we need to provide air-gap install archive / installation runbook and signed binaries. They also asked about model sizes: comfortable with 13B float -> prefer quantized 13B (int8/q4) for latency/cost; want comparison numbers vs 7B baseline.

Security: Must integrate with their HSM (SafeGuard HSM, PKCS#11) for model encryption keys and signing. Also need to demonstrate audit logs forwarded to their Splunk instance (on-prem). RBAC mapping: they use Active Directory; expect SAML/Okta federation for Redwood console access.

Operational gotchas (notes to self):
- Cold-start tokenization memory spikes; measure peak GPU memory for long prompts (>2048 tokens).
- Network egress locked down — bootstrap/download of model weights must be done via signed USB or internal mirror. Provide checksums and GPG-signed manifests.
- Per-device ephemeral KV cache strategy (for device isolation) might be required to avoid cross-patient leakage.
- Recovery story for model corruption when no internet: offline repair tools + local backup policy required.

Regulatory: they want a short artifact showing how Redwood Private supports HIPAA controls (BAA language examples) and an architecture diagram with data flow labels (PHI in/out). Ask legal for a BAA template with Private deployments.

Questions we need answers for (from Orchid):
- Expected concurrent sessions during peak (they said 10k daily, unclear concurrency) -> ask for P95 concurrency and average session length.
- Acceptable model latency SLOs per query under realistic prompt sizes (200–600 tokens typical) -> need sample prompts.
- Which internal CI/CD they will run for OS/security patches; do they require our installer to integrate with their configuration management (Ansible/CIS benchmarks)?

Internal decisions to make:
- Can we provide an air-gap installer flow that is supported by our Private team without expanding SLAs? (cost implications)
- We need a security review package (attestation, signed hashes, HSM integration doc) — owner: Priya.
- Quantization bench: produce 7B vs 13B vs 13B-q4 perf/cost matrix on A100 & H100. Owner: Diego.

tech_constraints: Air-gap means we cannot rely on hosted model hub. Need: (1) signed model artifacts tarball + manifest, (2) offline license/activation mechanism, (3) installer that accepts local path to artifacts. HSM integration must be via PKCS#11 and support rotating keys. If hospital uses older NVIDIA drivers, ensure runtime supports driver X.Y or provide container with correct drivers. Also evaluate whether we need to ship tokenizer tables locally or can derive them from model artefacts.
